cases.academic_assessment: A comparative-religion, culture and meaning concept was assessed first against the actual selected route. UCR has meaningful material on myth, religious visual culture, ancient religious identities, ethics and philosophical questions, but the course content cannot sustain a complete programme centred on comparative religious traditions and their study. The selected route requires World Religions, Christian history, Judaism, Islam, Hinduism, study-of-religion foundations, anthropology and psychology of religion, sacred-text hermeneutics, interreligious relations and comparative religious ethics, as well as the selected Islamic-history/philosophy units. Those are substantial subjects, not language or licensing requirements. A 24-course combination would increasingly depend on general philosophy, art history, sociology or politics without a specific content-level account of their contribution to this religion-centred concept. Religion/political conflict, sustainability, Islamic studies and confessional/practical theology were also considered; none solves that coherence problem. The no-match conclusion concerns the assembled programme, not the absence of a degree title or exact one-to-one course equivalents. The selected comparative Religie en Levensbeschouwing route is complete at 180 EC, including 30 EC genuine profiling space. Its Dutch part-time pacing remains six calendar years; compulsory Greek/Hebrew or a confessional route are not invented. The selected Islamic-history and Islamic-philosophy choices are retained. The comparative traditions, research labs and thesis remain required. Concrete course evidence and complete registry-row roles/candidate dispositions are preserved in the canonical exception. No UCR alternative is manufactured; this closes the pending UCR assessment without reopening external first-stage research.

cases.academic_assessment: A religion, cultural identity and political impact concept was tested against the selected broad specialisation. Several UCR courses illuminate religious myth, visual heritage, ancient identities, moral arguments and aspects of religious freedom or radicalisation. They do not supply a sustained inquiry into historical and lived Christianity, Judaism, Islam and South Asian traditions, religious experience and ritual, sacred texts and images, and religion-specific research methods. Replacing this 120-EC defining compulsory foundation with general political science, sociology, media analysis or psychology would leave the proposed curriculum centred on those general fields. The selected political-impact specialisation permits a focused related response, but it does not make incidental religious examples across unrelated courses a credible 24-course programme. Conflict/migration, environment, religious freedom, spiritual care and education directions were tested independently; none supplies the missing cumulative religion-centred study. This is an academic coherence decision, not a requirement to reproduce every external module or a professional qualification. The corrected ordinary 180-EC Groningen pathway retains 120 EC compulsory first-/second-year religion study, a 15-EC university/personal minor, two selected 7.5-EC faculty choices, the Cultural and Political Impact of Religion specialisation, thesis seminar, 10-EC thesis and 5-EC science communication. The 15-EC minor is not enlarged into 30 EC unrestricted choice, and optional education/spiritual-care routes are not stacked. Concrete course evidence and complete registry-row roles/candidate dispositions are preserved in the canonical exception. No UCR alternative is manufactured; this closes the pending UCR assessment without reopening external first-stage research.

prior_exception.curriculumContext: The current 2026–2027 Mechanical Engineering/Marine Technology OER, Marine curriculum table and BEP conditions (PDF pp.30–31), was freshly retrieved and visually inspected on 8 October 2026. Its ordinary requirements control over the live webpage older category allocation and chart. Year one comprises mathematics 12 EC, mechanics 24 EC, marine theory 16 EC and Integration and Skills 1/2 totaling 8 EC: 60. Year two comprises mathematics 12, Advanced Mechanics 6, Systems and Control Engineering 6, marine theory 18, Ship Design 6 and Integration and Skills 3 at 12: 60. Year three comprises a genuine 30-EC minor, Dynamics of Marine Structures 6, Electrical Drive and Conversion 4, Ship Motions and Manoeuvring 6 and Bachelor Final Project 14: 60. All 26 individual course/project/minor components total 180 EC. Integration and Skills 1/2/3 total 20 EC; Ship Design is a separate required 6-EC project within the listed 180, not an added duplicate. Mathematics and advanced-mechanics subparts remain embedded in their parent weights. Current MT1466-26 supersedes the older MT1466 code. The formal 14-EC final project replaces the old webpage 12-EC allocation. Its current entry requirement is all first-year courses and at least 54 second-year EC. No outdated ship-production/complex-loads category is carried into the current final-year list or independently added.

cases.academic_assessment: The closest concept—mathematical analysis and design of vessels and marine systems—was tested before adjacent directions. UCR provides substantial calculus, linear algebra, numerical methods, probability and linear-system analysis, plus useful computational and environmental methods. It does not provide a cumulative subject sequence in mechanics, thermodynamics, hydrostatics, hydromechanics, resistance/propulsion, marine structures, ship motions or vessel design. These are the objects to which the external mathematics and control methods are applied, not merely professional accreditation requirements. General algorithms, data science and sustainability courses cannot by themselves sustain 23 non-PPD courses centred on vessels and their integrated physical systems. Related sustainable-shipping, offshore/coastal and maritime-economic directions were assessed separately; each has some genuine UCR support, but extending it into a complete curriculum would shift the organising object to general environmental science, computing or economics without enough documented maritime-system content. The conclusion concerns coherence of a complete related programme, not exact module equivalence or absence of a Marine Technology degree title. The complete corrected external curriculum remains preserved. Concrete course evidence and four independently assessed candidate directions support a reasoned no-match exception; no UCR programme is manufactured.
